350224.title: Higher-dimensional Füredi–Hajnal conjecture
350224.literal_statement:
For $t\geq 2$, let $P$ be a $t$-pattern, and let $f_t(n,P)$ be the maximum number of $1$'s in a $t$-dimensional $n\times\cdots\times n$ $0$–$1$ matrix avoiding $P$. **Higher-dimensional Füredi–Hajnal conjecture.** The maximum number $f_t(n,P)$ of entries $1$ in a $t$-dimensional $n\times\cdots\times n$ $0$–$1$ matrix avoiding $P$ is bounded by

$$
a_P n^{t-1},
$$

where $a_P$ depends only on $P$. This generalizes the two-dimensional Füredi–Hajnal conjecture, whose linear bound is known to imply the Stanley–Wilf conjecture. The conjecture asks for the corresponding $n^{t-1}$ extremal bound in every dimension.
350224.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Recover the source definition of t-pattern before applying multidimensional permutation-pattern theorems. No source body read; no known-result exclusion inferred from the name.

350251.title: Sublinear type-2 growth for the identity into the smallest valid norm
350251.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a valid norm, meaning a norm on $\mathcal{S}_1^{\tilde k'\!, n}\otimes\mathcal{S}_1^{\tilde k'\!, n}\otimes\ell_2^{k\tilde k'}$ satisfying

$$
\|x\|_X\gtrsim\|x\|_{X^{iii}}
$$

for every $x$, together with

$$
\left\|\lvert i\rangle\otimes\lvert j\rangle\otimes\left(V\lvert ij\rangle\otimes\operatorname{Id}_{\ell_2^{\tilde k'}}\right)\right\|_X\leq1
$$

for every $V\in B_{M_{n^2k,\tilde k'}}$ and $i,j=1,\ldots,n$. Let $\operatorname{Id}:X\to X^{iii}$ be the identity map between the same underlying vector space equipped with these norms, and let $\mathrm{T}_2^{(n^2)}$ denote its type-2 constant restricted to $n^2$ vectors. **Identity-map conjecture.** There exists a valid norm $X$ and a dimension-independent constant $\beta<1$ such that

$$
\mathrm{T}_2^{(n^2)}\left(\operatorname{Id}:X\to X^{iii}\right)\lesssim_{\log}n^\beta.
$$

This is the final and weakest form proposed in the source; it would imply the desired lower bounds for position-based cryptography. No resolution is given.
350251.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Recover all tensor norms, valid-norm constants and log-loss quantifiers. Need dimension-uniform type2 estimate, not a fixed-dimensional certificate.

350266.title: Réti et al.'s maximum Sombor index conjecture for connected cyclic graphs
350266.literal_statement:
Let $n$ and $\nu$ be fixed integers with

$$
5\leq\nu\leq n-2.
$$

Let $H_{n,\nu}$ be the graph constructed from the star $S_n$ by adding $\nu$ edges between a fixed pendent vertex and $\nu$ other pendent vertices. The Sombor index of a graph $G$ is

$$
SO(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{\operatorname{deg}_G(u)^2+\operatorname{deg}_G(v)^2}.
$$

**Réti et al.'s conjecture.** Among all connected $\nu$-cyclic graphs of order $n$, only the graph $H_{n,\nu}$ has the maximum Sombor index.

The conjecture identifies the unique extremal graph for the Sombor index in this class. It is proved in Section 3 of the source paper.
350266.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Existing source Theorem3.5 proves the exact conjecture, indeed range0<=nu<=n-2. Actual proof and local majorization lemmas inspected; cited predecessor not independently audited.

350275.title: Frankl–Tokushige's forbidden-intersection conjecture
350275.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$, and let $\ell$ be an integer with $2\ell<k$. Suppose that every pair $F,F'\in\mathcal{F}$ satisfies $|F\cap F'|\ne\ell$. **Frankl–Tokushige's conjecture.** Then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\le\binom{n}{k-\ell-1}.
$$

This is a forbidden-intersection problem: it asks for the largest $k$-uniform family avoiding one prescribed intersection size, and the paper presents a partial result toward the conjectured bound.
350275.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Source Conjecture2 and Theorem10 proof read. Polynomial method handles k-ell not dividing ell!, plus source-known prime-power cases. Need the residual cases; no full-scope proof.

350277.title: Eigenvector delocalization conjecture for random graph walks
350277.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be the random graph and let $\nu_1,\dots,\nu_n$ be the eigenvectors appearing in Theorem 1 of the paper, with $p$ as in that theorem. For a vector $v$, write $\|v\|_\infty$ for its largest coordinate in absolute value. **Eigenvector delocalization conjecture.** With probability converging to $1$ as $n\to\infty$,

$$
\max_{k=2,\dots,n}\|\nu_k\|_\infty^2=o\left(\sqrt{\frac{p}{n}}\right).
$$

This conjecture would provide the eigenvector delocalization estimate needed to show that the relevant eigenvector sum is negligible on the paper's scale. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
350277.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Recover random-graph p-range and eigenvector normalization in Theorem1. Need uniform high-probability delocalization at the stated scale; no fixed-graph counterexample qualifies.

350295.title: Cioabă and Wong's spectral spanning-tree packing conjecture
350295.literal_statement:
Let $m\geq 1$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph with $d\geq 2m+2$. Let $\lambda_2(G)$ be the second-largest adjacency eigenvalue of $G$, and let $\sigma(G)$ denote the maximum number of edge-disjoint spanning trees in $G$. **Cioabă and Wong's conjecture.** If

$$
\lambda_2(G)<d-\frac{2m+1}{d+1},
$$

then

$$
\sigma(G)\geq m+1.
$$

This conjecture gives a factor-of-two improvement over the earlier spectral condition implying the existence of $m+1$ edge-disjoint spanning trees; it was verified for $m\in\{1,2\}$, while the paper constructs examples showing that the conjectured bound is essentially best possible.
350295.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need a uniform spectral cut/partition argument reaching m+1 spanning trees; source body and later resolutions not checked. Small m cases explicitly already known in the record.

350316.title: Sperner conjecture for the posets $P_{n,l}$
350316.literal_statement:
Let $P_{n,l}$ be the poset defined in the paper, with parameters $n$ and $l$ satisfying

$$
0\leq l<n.
$$

A poset is **Sperner** if its largest antichain has cardinality equal to the largest rank size. **Sperner conjecture.** For $0\leq l<n$, the poset $P_{n,l}$ is Sperner.

The preceding theorem shows that $P_{n,l}$ is rank-log-concave, providing evidence for the conjecture; whether every such $P_{n,l}$ is Sperner is left open here.
350316.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Three mechanisms attempted: adjacent-rank matching, balanced uniform flows, source insertion-weight extension. Finite matchings/flows pass; simple source formula fails at ell2. Need universal Hall/normalized-flow lemma. See ATTEMPTS.md.

350338.title: Extraneous-mode conjecture for the type B twisted W-algebra module
350338.literal_statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer, let $\epsilon(i)$ denote the twist shift for the strong generators, and define the positive modes

$$
S_+ = \{\mathsf{W}^i_k\mid i\in [2r],\ k\in(\mathbb{Z}_{>0}-\epsilon(i))\}.
$$

Set $S'=\{\mathsf{W}^{2r-1}_{1/2}\}\subset S_+$. **Type B extraneous-mode conjecture.** The subset $S'$ is extraneous in the sense of the source's definition. This condition is needed to construct the shifted Airy structure whose partition function gives the desired Whittaker vector; the source states that the relevant subalgebra condition is known, but that existence of this extraneous subset has not been proved for the twisted module.
350338.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Extraneous-mode definition and twisted-module action not recovered from primary body. Metadata reference solved label is unsupported by its quoted unrelated sentence; no resolution asserted.

350376.title: Welzl's minimum partial triangulations conjecture
350376.literal_statement: Let $W_n$ be the number of full or partial triangulations of a convex $n$-gon, with $W_2=1$. For a set of $n$ points in the plane in general position, a partial triangulation is a noncrossing set of diagonals whose addition decomposes the convex hull into triangles and possibly polygons. **Welzl's minimum partial triangulations conjecture.** Convex $n$-gons minimize the number of partial triangulations among all point sets in general position; equivalently, every set of $n$ points in the plane in general position has at least $W_n$ partial triangulations. This conjecture asks whether the convex configuration is extremal for counting partial triangulations of planar point sets; the supplied source does not give evidence of a resolution.
350376.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Recover exact partial-triangulation convention and whether unused points are allowed; then prove convex lower bound or give certified point configuration violating it. No source body read.

350380.title: Subcubic multigraph star chromatic index conjecture
350380.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic multigraph, meaning a multigraph with maximum degree at most $3$. The star chromatic index $\chi'_{\mathrm{star}}(G)$ is the smallest number of colors in a proper edge coloring of $G$ with no bichromatic path or cycle of length four.

**Subcubic multigraph star chromatic index conjecture.**

$$
\chi'_{\mathrm{star}}(G)\le 6.
$$

The previously known upper bound is $7$. The conjecture was posed by Dvořák, Mohar, and Šámal and remains open.
350380.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need six-color star edge coloring for all source-allowed subcubic multigraphs or a seven-required loopless example. Loop/domain corrections cannot qualify; primary scope unresolved.

350390.title: Karasev's smallest-solid-angle conjecture for simplices
350390.literal_statement: Let ${\mathcal P}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a $d$-dimensional simplex, and let its solid angle be measured in the usual way. **Karasev's smallest-solid-angle conjecture.** Every $d$-dimensional simplex has a solid angle not greater than that of the $d$-dimensional regular simplex. The conjecture concerns the simplex minimizing the solid angle among $d$-dimensional simplices and remains open in dimensions $d\geq 5$.
350390.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need full arbitrary-dimensional minimum-angle comparison. Source solid-angle normalization and high-dimensional reductions uninspected; no new endpoint.

350409.title: Harrington–Henninger-Voss–Karhadkar–Robinson–Wong sum–difference index equality conjecture
350409.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. Its sum index, denoted by $\operatorname{sum}(G)$, is the minimum number of distinct values of $f(u)+f(v)$ over the edges $uv$ among injective labellings $f:V(G)\to\mathbb{Z}$. Its difference index, denoted by $\operatorname{dif}(G)$, is defined analogously using $|f(u)-f(v)|$. **Harrington–Henninger-Voss–Karhadkar–Robinson–Wong's conjecture.** Every nonempty simple graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{dif}(G)=\left\lceil\operatorname{sum}(G)/2\right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture was motivated by exact computations for several graph families and is false: the paper constructs counterexamples in which the conjectured value is arbitrarily far from the truth in either direction.
350409.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Existing source Theorem2.2 chain-of-odd-cycles construction refutes exact Conjecture1.1. Read cycle-label counting proof and construction. No new finite-witness credit.

350413.title: Carlson et al.'s Shearer-type surplus conjecture for clique-free graphs
350413.literal_statement:
Let $r\ge 3$ be fixed. A graph is **$d$-degenerate** if every subgraph has a vertex of degree at most $d$, and $K_r$ denotes the complete graph on $r$ vertices. For a graph with $m$ edges, let its surplus be the quantity measuring the excess of its maximum cut over the baseline determined by its number of edges.

**Carlson et al.'s conjecture.** Every $K_r$-free $d$-degenerate graph with $m$ edges has surplus

$$
\Omega_r\left(\frac{m}{\sqrt{d}}\right).
$$

Carlson et al. proposed this as an analogue of Shearer's bound for $K_r$-free graphs and showed that it would imply the conjecture of Alon, Bollobás, Krivelevich and Sudakov on surplus in $H$-free graphs. The supplied material does not state whether this conjecture has been resolved.
350413.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need source surplus normalization and uniform degenerate clique-free estimate; no concrete certificate or full-scope bridge established. Primary definitions unresolved.

350441.title: The explicit matroid construction conjecture
350441.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid and $K$ a lift of $M$. Let $\mathcal{C}(M)$ denote the set of circuits of $M$. Define $\mathcal{I}$ to be the collection of subsets $\mathcal{C}'\subseteq\mathcal{C}(M)$ for which there is no matroid $K'$ such that $K'$ is a projection of $K$ and a lift of $M$, every set in $\mathcal{C}'$ is a circuit of $K'$, and

$$
r(K)-r(K')<|\mathcal{C}'|.
$$

**The explicit matroid construction conjecture.** The collection $\mathcal{I}$ is the collection of independent sets of a matroid $N$ on $\mathcal{C}(M)$, and

$$
K\cong M^N.
$$

This conjecture would explicitly construct the matroid required by the general lift construction conjecture. It is presented as open.
350441.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need source lift/projection and M^N definitions, then independence exchange for every allowed lift, or finite matroid counterexample with all projection quantifiers. No primary body read.

350470.title: Dihedral-family conjecture for non-axisymmetric critical points of the Onsager potential
350470.literal_statement: Consider the Onsager potential with interaction parameter $\mu>0$. For a positive integer $n$, let $D^{2n\mathrm{h}}$ denote the relevant horizontal dihedral symmetry group, and call a critical point **non-axisymmetric** when it lacks axial symmetry. **Dihedral-family conjecture.** There exists a non-axisymmetric critical point with $D^{2n\mathrm{h}}$ symmetry for some $\mu>0$. Numerical computations exhibit several non-axisymmetric states with discrete symmetries, while the asserted existence for the stated dihedral family is not proved in the supplied material.
350470.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Recover the n-quantifier, potential kernel, group action and non-axisymmetry requirement. Existence of a discretely symmetric stationary density requires analytic bridge, not numerical critical points.

350493.title: Non-perfectness conjecture for generating graphs of finite simple groups
350493.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite non-abelian simple group. Its generating graph $\Gamma(G)$ has the elements of $G$ as vertices, with two vertices adjacent when they generate $G$. A graph is **perfect** if every induced subgraph has chromatic number equal to its clique number.

**Non-perfectness conjecture.** The generating graph $\Gamma(G)$ is not perfect.

The conjecture is motivated by the result that $\Gamma(A_n)$ and $\Gamma(S_n)$ are perfect exactly when $n<5$, while $A_5$ is the smallest 2-generated finite group whose generating graph is not perfect. The conjecture remains open in the source.
350493.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need an induced odd hole/antihole in every finite nonabelian simple-group generating graph or a perfect counterexample. Family/classification scope and prior work unread.

350496.title: W[1]-hardness of M-EPVCB parameterized by the smaller bipartition
350496.literal_statement: Let $G=(X,Y,E)$ be the edge-weighted bipartite graph in an instance of M-EPVCB, and let $|X|$ and $|Y|$ denote the sizes of its two bipartition classes. **The minimum-side hardness conjecture.** M-EPVCB is W[1]-hard with respect to the parameter $\min\{|X|,|Y|\}$. This would strengthen the known W[1]-hardness result parameterized by $k_1$; the conjecture is posed as a question for future work and remains unresolved in the supplied source.
350496.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Recover M-EPVCB decision problem and weighted encoding, then a parameter-preserving W1 reduction. Neither a runtime diagnostic nor finite example proves the hardness claim.

350508.title: Connectedness conjecture for the complement of the zero-locus
350508.literal_statement:
For each integer $\Delta\geq 3$, let $\mathcal{G}_\Delta$ be the class of graphs of maximum degree at most $\Delta$, and let

$$
\mathcal{Z}_\Delta=\{\lambda\in\mathbb{C}:Z_G(\lambda)=0\text{ for some }G\in\mathcal{G}_\Delta\},
$$

where $Z_G(\lambda)$ is the independence polynomial of $G$ evaluated at $\lambda$. The **connectedness conjecture.** For each integer $\Delta\geq 3$, the set

$$
\mathbb{C}\setminus\overline{\mathcal{Z}_\Delta}
$$

is connected. The topology of the complement of the zero-locus is not understood; resolving this conjecture would clarify the global structure of the zero-free region relevant to approximating the independence polynomial.
350508.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need global connectedness outside closure of all bounded-degree independence roots; finite polynomial root plots cannot certify this infinite union. Source body unread.

350528.title: Rainbow directed cycle-or-path conjecture for proper arc-colourings
350528.literal_statement: Let $\overleftrightarrow{K_n}$ be the digraph obtained from the complete graph $K_n$ by replacing each edge with two oppositely directed arcs and adding a directed loop at each vertex. A **proper arc-colouring** is a colouring in which no two arcs of the same colour have a common head or a common tail. **Rainbow directed cycle-or-path conjecture.** Every proper arc-colouring of $\overleftrightarrow{K_n}$ admits a rainbow directed cycle or path of length at least $n-1$. This conjecture is motivated by bounds for rainbow directed cycles and by the study of connected rainbow subgraphs with maximum in-degree and out-degree at most one; it remains open.
350528.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need rainbow directed path or cycle of length>=n-1 for all proper arc colourings with source loop conventions. Primary quantifiers unresolved; no small witness nominated.

350532.title: Extremal Betti-number conjecture for random higher-degree monomial ideals
350532.literal_statement:
Fix integers $d,m$ with $d\geq m\geq 1$, and suppose that $\alpha$ satisfies

$$
\frac{1}{\binom{d+1}{m}}<\alpha<\frac{1}{\binom{d}{m}}.
$$

Let $\Delta\sim\Delta_m(n,n^{-\alpha})$ be the corresponding multiparameter random simplicial complex, and let $I_\Delta$ be its Stanley–Reisner ideal. **Extremal Betti-number conjecture.** With high probability,

$$
\mathbb{Q}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/I_\Delta
$$

has regularity and depth both equal to $d+1$, and has one extremal Betti number, namely $\beta_{n-(d+1),n}$. The conjecture proposes that random squarefree monomial ideals generated in fixed degree exhibit algebraic behavior analogous to random quadratic monomial ideals, but its validity is left open in the source.
350532.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need source random-complex distribution, regularity/depth conventions and characteristic hypotheses; full high-probability asymptotic theorem required. No source body read.

350537.title: Uniqueness conjecture for invariant Ricci solitons on the four-sphere
350537.literal_statement:
Let $(g,u)$ be an $SO(2)\times SO(3)$-invariant solution of the gradient Ricci soliton equation on $\mathbb{S}^4$ with soliton constant $\lambda=1$. The equation is understood with respect to the metric $g$ and potential function $u$.

**Uniqueness conjecture.** Any such solution is the round sphere, up to diffeomorphism.

The conjecture seeks to determine uniqueness among invariant shrinking Ricci solitons on $\mathbb{S}^4$. The paper proves a compactness result for these solutions, including uniform injectivity-radius, volume, and pointwise curvature bounds, but the stated uniqueness remains open.
350537.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need invariant metric/potential ODE and smooth pole conditions; constant-potential normalization corrections cannot qualify. Full geometric uniqueness remains unattempted.

350552.title: Dimension-stability conjecture for exact hypercube covering numbers
350552.literal_statement:
For $B\subset\{0,1\}^k$ and an integer $n\geq k$, let $\operatorname{ec}(B)$ be the minimum number of hyperplanes whose union intersects the Boolean cube precisely in $B$. **Dimension-stability conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ec}\bigl(\{0,1\}^{n}\setminus(B\times\{0\}^{n-k})\bigr)=n-k+\operatorname{ec}\bigl(\{0,1\}^{k}\setminus B\bigr).
$$

The right-hand side is an immediate upper bound obtained by extending a cover in $k$ dimensions and adding the $n-k$ coordinate hyperplanes. The conjecture asks whether embedding the problem in higher dimensions can ever improve this bound; the source gives no resolution.

350573.title: The weighted Erdős matching conjecture for overlapping families
350573.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer and let $vec{p}=(p,1,\ldots,1)$. For $n\geq (s+1)k$, define $f_{vec{p}}(n,k,s)$ as the maximum weighted sum associated with $s+1$ overlapping families of $k$-subsets of $[n]$, with weights given by $vec{p}$. **Weighted Erdős matching conjecture.**

$$
f_{vec{p}}(n,k,s) = \max \left\{ s\binom{n}{k}, (p+s) \binom{(s+1)k-1}{k},(p+s)\left(\binom{n}{k}-\binom{n-s}{k}\right)\right\}.
$$

The conjecture would imply all the results in the paper and, in the special case where all the families coincide, the Erdős matching conjecture. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
350573.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Recover weighted overlapping-family definition and all n,k,s,p ranges; need uniform extremal theorem or source-valid strict violation. No source body read.

350588.title: Bessy–Havet extremal 3-edge-coloring conjecture for connected cubic graphs
350588.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected cubic graph of order $n$, meaning that $G$ has $n$ vertices, and let a **3-edge-coloring** assign three colors to the edges so that incident edges receive different colors.

**Bessy–Havet extremal coloring conjecture.** The connected cubic graph of order $n$ with the largest number of 3-edge-colorings has

$$
\frac{2^{n/2-1}+4}{3}
$$

3-edge-colorings if $n/2$ is even and

$$
\frac{2^{n/2-1}+2}{3}
$$

3-edge-colorings if $n/2$ is odd.

The paper attributes this conjecture to Bessy and Havet and notes the known upper bound $3\cdot 2^{n/2-3}$ for the number of 3-edge-colorings of a connected cubic graph. The stated extremal formula remains open in the supplied text.
350588.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Recover counting modulo color permutations and simplicity conventions; displayed fractions are not an invitation to a normalization counterexample. No primary body read.

350596.title: The chordal graph k-path vertex cover conjecture
350596.literal_statement:
Let $k\ge 3$, let $G$ be a chordal graph with clique number $\omega$, and write $n=|V(G)|$. Let $\psi_k(G)$ denote the minimum size of a vertex set meeting every path on $k$ vertices in $G$.

**Chordal graph k-path vertex cover conjecture.**

$$
\psi_k(G) \le \frac{\omega-1}{\omega+k-2}n.
$$

The authors present this as a hoped-for improvement to some of the paper's bounds for chordal graphs. No resolution is given in the supplied text.

350602.title: Super-polynomial one-color oriented Ramsey growth for bounded-degree acyclic digraphs
350602.literal_statement:
For $k,\Delta\geq 1$ and $n>\Delta$, let $H_{k,n,\Delta}$ be an acyclic digraph with $n$ vertices and maximum degree $\Delta$ maximizing $\ovar{r_k}(H)$. **Super-polynomial growth conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $\Delta$ such that

$$
\ovar{r_1}(H_{1,n,\Delta})\geq n^{\omega(1)}.
$$

The paper establishes polynomial lower bounds and super-polynomial lower bounds for at least two colors, but leaves this one-color case open.
350602.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need bounded-degree infinite family with one-color oriented Ramsey number superpolynomial in n. Finite extremal tournaments cannot settle asymptotic quantifiers. No source body read.

350603.title: Quantitative growth conjecture for multicolor oriented Ramsey numbers
350603.literal_statement:
For $k,\Delta\geq 1$ and $n>\Delta$, let $H_{k,n,\Delta}$ be an acyclic digraph with $n$ vertices and maximum degree $\Delta$ maximizing $\ovar{r_k}(H)$. **Quantitative growth conjecture.** There exist $\Delta\geq 3$ and constants $c_k=\omega_k(1)$ and $C_k=2^{o(k)}$ such that

$$
\Omega(\log^{c_k} n)\leq \log \ovar{r_k}(H_{k,n,\Delta})\leq O(\log^{C_k} n).
$$

This is proposed as a quantitative refinement of the open question of determining the logarithmic order of these Ramsey numbers; the source gives no resolution evidence.
350603.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need precise source asymptotic meaning in n,k and constants c_k,C_k; full two-sided theorem or incompatible family, not a fixed k variant. No primary body read.

350605.title: Super-polynomial directed Ramsey numbers with three colors
350605.literal_statement:
Let $\overleftrightarrow{r_3}(H)$ be the three-color directed Ramsey number, and let an acyclic digraph have maximum degree at most $\Delta$. **Three-color directed-Ramsey conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $\Delta$ and an infinite sequence $\{H_n\}$ of $n$-vertex acyclic digraphs, each with maximum degree at most $\Delta$, such that

$$
\overleftrightarrow{r_3}(H_n)\geq n^{\omega(1)}.
$$

The paper notes super-polynomial constructions for some other numbers of colors but identifies the three-color case as an unresolved intermediate case.
350605.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need a bounded-degree infinite sequence with the three-color directed growth; source conventions not recovered. No finite-order diagnostic could qualify alone.

350620.title: Positivity conjecture for the multivariate Bessel addition law
350620.literal_statement:
Let $\theta>0$, and let $\a=(a_1\le\dots\le a_N)$ and $\b=(b_1\le\dots\le b_N)$ be $N$-tuples. The distribution $\c=\a+_\theta\b$ is defined through the multivariate Bessel identity

$$
\mathbb E B_{(c_1,\dots,c_N)}(x_1,\dots,x_N;\,\theta)=B_{(a_1,\dots,a_N)}(x_1,\dots,x_N;\,\theta)B_{(b_1,\dots,b_N)}(x_1,\dots,x_N;\,\theta).
$$

**Positivity conjecture.** For every such $\a$ and $\b$, there exists a probability measure on $N$-tuples $\c=(c_1\le\dots\le c_N)$ satisfying the identity for all $x_1,\dots,x_N\in\mathbb C$.

The identity is known to define a compactly supported generalized function or distribution of total mass $1$, but it is not known in general whether this distribution is positive and hence a probability measure. The conjecture would provide a probabilistic interpretation of the Bessel addition law and is relevant to addition problems for general beta random matrices.
350620.mathematical_attempt_and_remaining_lemma: Need full multivariate Bessel definition and positive addition distribution for arbitrary theta,N or a certified negative moment functional. Classical matrix beta cases are insufficient; no primary body read.

350625.title: The largest-legal-weight strategy conjecture for Staller
350625.literal_statement: Let a **partial covering function** be a current position in the fractional transversal game from which legal submoves are defined. **Largest-legal-weight strategy conjecture.** Starting from any partial covering function, there is an optimal strategy for Staller such that, in every submove, she always spends the largest legal weight. The paper presents this as a stronger version of the integer-move conjecture, with no resolution given.

350635.title: Belkhechine et al.'s lower-bound conjecture for maximum inversion number
350635.literal_statement:
For a positive integer $n$, define

$$
\operatorname{inv}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{inv}(D)\mid D\text{ is an oriented graph of order }n\}.
$$

By monotonicity, this is also the maximum over tournaments of order $n$.

**Belkhechine et al.'s lower-bound conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{inv}(n)\geq\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This is proposed as a strengthening of the general counting lower bound for the maximum inversion number. The conjecture is attributed in the paper to Belkhechine et al.

350636.title: The inversion number of the Hamiltonian-path reversal tournament
350636.literal_statement:
Let $Q_n$ be the tournament obtained from the transitive tournament of order $n$ by reversing the arcs of its unique directed Hamiltonian path $(v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n)$. Let $\operatorname{inv}(Q_n)$ denote its inversion number.

**Hamiltonian-path reversal conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{inv}(Q_n)=\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This is presented as an explicit family expected to attain the conjectured lower bound for the maximum inversion number. The claim is attributed in the paper to Belkhechine et al.

350651.title: Finiteness conjecture for 2-unavoidable doubled patterns
350651.literal_statement:
A pattern is a word over an alphabet of variables, and it is **doubled** if every variable occurs at least twice. Its avoidability index is the smallest alphabet size of an infinite word avoiding the pattern; a doubled pattern is **2-unavoidable** when no infinite word over a $2$-letter alphabet avoids it.

**Finiteness conjecture for 2-unavoidable doubled patterns.** There exist only finitely many $2$-unavoidable doubled patterns.

This conjecture is stated as related to, but independent of, the conjecture that every square-free doubled pattern is $2$-avoidable. The supplied text gives no resolution.

350683.title: Immersion number conjecture for generalized Mycielski graphs of complete graphs
350683.literal_statement:
For integers $m\geq 3$, let $K_{m+1}$ be the complete graph on $m+1$ vertices, let $\mu_m(K_{m+1})$ be its $m$-Mycielskian, and let $\operatorname{im}(G)$ denote the largest $t$ such that $G$ has a $K_t$-immersion. **Immersion number conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{im}\bigl(\mu_m(K_{m+1})\bigr)=2m+1.
$$

The conjecture arises from examples showing unusually large immersion numbers for generalized Mycielski graphs, including $\operatorname{im}(\mu_3(K_4))=7$ and $\operatorname{im}(\mu_4(K_5))=9$. The source does not provide a resolution.

350735.title: The simplicial volume conjecture for open 3-manifolds
350735.literal_statement:
Let $SV(3)$ be the set of simplicial volumes of closed $3$-manifolds, and let $SV^{\text{lf}}(3)$ be the set of simplicial volumes of all $3$-manifolds without boundary. Here simplicial volume is understood in the locally finite sense for open manifolds, and $\infty$ denotes infinite simplicial volume.

**Simplicial volume conjecture for open 3-manifolds.**

$$
SV^{\text{lf}}(3)=SV(3)\cup\{\infty\}.
$$

The equality would completely determine the set of simplicial volumes of open $3$-manifolds. The corresponding result is known for tame open $3$-manifolds, but the general case remains open.

350791.title: Campos–de Mello total coloring conjecture for powers of cycles
350791.literal_statement:
Let $C_n^k$ be the $k$th power of the cycle on $n$ vertices, with $2\leq k<\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Its maximum degree is denoted by $\Delta(C_n^k)$, and $\chi”(C_n^k)$ is its total chromatic number.

**Campos–de Mello's conjecture.** If $G=C_n^k$, then

$$
\chi”(G)=\begin{cases}
\Delta(G)+2, & \text{if } k>\frac{n}{3}-1 \text{ and } n \text{ is odd},\\
\Delta(G)+1, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

The source states that the total coloring conjecture has been verified for some even-order powers of cycles and that these graphs admit polynomial-time total colorings, while the displayed classification remains presented as a conjecture. The source gives no resolution status for this classification.

350792.title: Finite-certificate conjecture for relaxation complexity in dimension three
350792.literal_statement:
Let $X \subseteq \mathds{Z}^3$ be a **full-dimensional lattice-convex set**, and let $\operatorname{rc}(X,Y)$ denote the relaxation complexity of $X$ relative to a finite set $Y \subseteq \mathds{Z}^3 \setminus X$.

**Finite-certificate conjecture.** There exists a finite set $Y \subseteq \mathds{Z}^3 \setminus X$ such that

$$
\operatorname{rc}(X)=\operatorname{rc}(X,Y).
$$

The preceding result gives a lower bound for the relaxation complexity of full-dimensional lattice-convex sets in dimension three, but does not provide a finite certificate for its exact value. This conjecture asserts that such a finite certificate always exists in dimension three.

350801.title: Zilber–Pink finiteness conjecture for optimal subvarieties
350801.literal_statement:
Let $S$ be a Shimura variety and let $V$ be a subvariety of $S$. For an irreducible subvariety $W$ of $S$, let $\langle W\rangle$ be the smallest special subvariety of $S$ containing $W$, and define its defect by

$$
\delta(W)=\dim\langle W\rangle-\dim W.
$$

Call an irreducible subvariety $W$ of $V$ **optimal** in $V$ if, whenever $W\subsetneq Y$ for another irreducible subvariety $Y$ of $V$, one has $\delta(W)<\delta(Y)$; write $\operatorname{Opt}(V)$ for the set of optimal subvarieties of $V$. **Zilber–Pink conjecture.** The set $\operatorname{Opt}(V)$ is finite. This is an equivalent formulation of the central unlikely-intersections problem for Shimura varieties, and the paper studies effective results for related weakly optimal loci.
